recognize_zh: 高倍抹片中箭頭所指的紅血球有些邊緣出現透明的水泡樣區（blister cells）或咬痕狀缺口（bite cells），也有不少帶棘突的變形紅血球，提示氧化性溶血；在Wilson disease由銅離子引起。
features: Low power: moderate anisopoikilocytosis with scattered neutrophils and a lymphocyte (A)
Blister cells with hemoglobin retracted to one side leaving a clear membrane vesicle (B, arrowheads)
Bite-like cells with notched eccentric defects (B)
Several spiculated red cells (echinocytes/acanthocytes) and irregularly contracted cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows moderate anisopoikilocytosis. At higher magnification, numerous red cells show blister formation with eccentrically retracted hemoglobin and clear membrane vesicles, as well as bite-like notched defects (arrowheads), accompanied by spiculated echinocytic and acanthocytic forms. A polychromatic macrocyte indicates a reticulocyte response. Findings are consistent with oxidative hemolysis, which in this clinical context is attributable to copper-mediated injury in Wilson disease.

ddx.vs: Morphology is identical (bite and blister cells); separation requires G6PD enzyme assay and serum copper/ceruloplasmin studies.
Morphology overlaps; the discriminator is exposure history and methemoglobin level rather than smear features.
MAHA shows schistocytes (helmet and triangular fragments) with thrombocytopenia, not blister cells with retracted hemoglobin.

ddx.dx: Liver disease with spur cell anemia
ddx.vs: Spur cell anemia shows predominant acanthocytes with irregular spicules and lacks blister and bite cells.
